_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Craftsman Automation, consolidated, Rs crore, Screener basis. Revenue growth and EBITDA margin come from the three-segment build below (segment EBIT, as the company reports it), synced by CRAFTSMAN.ctx.js: EBITDA = sum of segment EBIT - unallocated corporate costs + depreciation. The Rs2,000 cr QIP of 18-Jun-2026 is in the Mar-26 opening balance sheet (CRAFTSMAN.patch.js) and all per-share figures use the post-QIP 2.6154 cr shares.
_revenueWhy: From the segment build. FY27E +24%: Q1FY27 was +36% (powertrain +26%, aluminium +38%, industrial +53%); management guided 'mid-teens' in May-2026 at then aluminium prices and indicated ~Rs6,500 cr of aluminium revenue (not guidance); Sunbeam exits may cut its revenue 10-20%. FY28E-29E: aluminium capacity (Hosur, DR Axion Sriperumbudur from FY28) and the large-engine castings ramp (~30% / 50% of a US$100 mn run-rate in FY28 / FY29).
_marginWhy: From the segment build: segment EBIT margins plus depreciation. FY26 15.3%, Q1FY27 15.8% (Screener basis). Sunbeam to mid-teens EBITDA by Q4FY27 (from single digits) lifts aluminium; new capacity at low utilisation and large-engine start-up costs hold it back.
_capexWhy: FY27: management's ~Rs1,500 cr ('conservatively': standalone >Rs1,000 cr, DR Axion ~Rs430 cr, Sunbeam maintenance), Q1FY27 call. FY28-29: the ~Rs1,000 cr standalone run-rate plus the DR Axion spill-over, then lower as plants fill (maintenance alone Rs250-300 cr). FY24-26 actual: Rs631 / 992 / 1,188 cr.
_depWhy: FY26 Rs444 cr on an average gross block of Rs6,473 cr (6.9%); the gross block includes Rs1,190 cr of land, which is not depreciated, and the engine depreciates capex at once (CWIP flat). 6.3% gives ~Rs500 cr in FY27E, matching Q1FY27's Rs120 cr a quarter plus new plants ('close to Rs500 cr', CMD).
_treasuryWhy: Net debt even after the QIP (Rs1,430 cr pro forma at Mar-26 on Screener's basis: borrowings incl. leases Rs3,623 cr less cash Rs179 cr, investments Rs14 cr and the Rs2,000 cr QIP), so no treasury yield; interest on the QIP cash until it is spent is in otherIncome.
_otherIncomeWhy: Built, not plugged. FY26 Rs61 cr (AR note 2.2): deposit interest Rs4.8 cr, forex gain Rs27.4 cr (rupee fell to ~95/US$), asset-sale gain Rs14.3 cr (one-off), rent and others Rs14.9 cr. FY27E Rs75 cr = interest on undeployed QIP cash (~Rs700 cr on average at ~6.5% = ~Rs45 cr) + recurring rent/others ~Rs15 cr + forex ~Rs15 cr. Reconciles to Q1FY27 Rs24 cr (x4 = Rs95 cr) and the four quarters to Jun-26 (Rs81 cr). FY28-29E: the QIP cash is spent, so ~Rs45 / 40 cr.
_interestWhy: FY26 Rs309 cr on gross debt that rose from Rs2,358 cr to Rs3,623 cr (incl. leases); Q1FY27 Rs86 cr (Rs344 cr annualised) before the QIP. Part of the QIP prepays debt, but capex of Rs1,500 cr keeps gross debt near Rs3,000 cr: ~Rs72 cr a quarter from Q2 (FY27E Rs300 cr), then Rs280 / 270 cr as net debt / EBITDA falls towards 1.5x.
_taxWhy: FY26 28% (Sunbeam's losses carry no tax credit), Q1FY27 25%; India 25.2% plus German and loss-making units. Falls as Sunbeam turns profitable.
_payoutWhy: FY26 payout 7%, FY25 6%, FY24 8% (Screener): the company keeps cash for capex.

build._note: Segment build (Rs crore). FY26 base = AR FY26 segment note. Segment EBIT is before unallocable corporate costs, other income and finance cost. Checked against model revenue and EBITDA in CRAFTSMAN.ctx.js.
build._why: Powertrain: Q1FY27 +26% from a weak base; CMD says it 'has come to a normal situation'; utilisation ~70%, truck demand muted, farm better; +15% in FY27-28, +18% in FY29 as large-engine castings reach ~50% of US$100 mn (~Rs475 cr). EBIT margin 16.6% in FY26, 18.3% in Q1FY27: 17.5% / 17.0% (large-engine start-up, lines at ~10% use) / 17.5%. Aluminium: FY27 +28% (Q1 +38%; Q2-Q4 ~Rs1,500-1,580 cr a quarter vs Rs1,203-1,310 cr a year earlier; Sunbeam exits lose 10-20% of its revenue); +16% / +14% as Hosur and the DR Axion plant fill. EBIT margin 10.3% in FY26, 10.1% in Q1: 10.6% / 11.3% / 11.8% (Sunbeam's turnaround, offset by new-plant depreciation; CMD: no 100-200bp gain 'at this rate'). Industrial & Engineering: Q1 +53% on material handling and storage ('not a one-time spike'); +25% / 15% / 12%; EBIT 4.4% in FY26, 9.1% in Q1: 8% / 8.5% / 8.5%. Unallocated corporate cost Rs110 cr in FY26 (Rs96 cr FY25); ~Rs30 cr in Q1FY27: Rs125 / 140 / 155 cr.

dcf._betaWhy: Cyclical CV, tractor and auto volumes, aluminium-price pass-through lags and a capex-heavy model: beta 1.1 (Ke 13.1%). After the QIP, net debt is ~5% of enterprise value, so a WACC would be only ~0.3pp lower; the engine discounts at the cost of equity (see the sensitivity grid).
dcf._tgWhy: House range 5-6%: 6% (India manufacturing and outsourcing by global OEMs keep growth above vehicle volumes).
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~15% to 8% over 15 years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin ~16.5% in steady state (FY22-26 range 15-24%; mix has shifted to lower-margin aluminium).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex 6.5% of revenue in steady state (FY22-26: 10-17%, a build-out phase); depreciation 5.5%.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Aluminium wins (Hosur, DR Axion's new plant, exports) fill capacity faster, Sunbeam reaches mid-teens EBITDA on time, large-engine castings ramp a year early and the industrial upcycle lasts: growth ~4pp a year higher and EBITDA margin +0.8pp.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: A CV and tractor downturn, aluminium price swings that customers pass through late, Sunbeam's turnaround slipping and new plants running half empty: growth ~5pp a year lower and EBITDA margin -1.5pp.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Craftsman: P/E on FY28E EPS (Motilal Oswal 28x FY28E, 30-Jul-2026; Emkay uses EV/EBITDA). Multiple derived in CRAFTSMAN.ctx.js (own forward-P/E median x the auto-component de-rating) and written by syncMultiples().

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Emkay's method (17x Jun-28E EV/EBITDA). Our multiple: own trailing EV/EBITDA median x the sector de-rating, restated from trailing to Sep-28E EBITDA; net debt deducted.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: 15-year FCFF at Ke 13.1% and 6% terminal growth, less net debt (QIP cash included).
